title: Registry
description: The artifact a Worker fetches to learn which Workflows it can run (ADR-0007). It names the Workflows this repo owns, carries each one's Node graph in API format, and declares the Parameters that graph exposes. Generated from the exports by registry/generate.py and never hand-written; validation of what a schema cannot express - that a Parameter's target really exists in the graph naming it - lives in generate.py's problems(). A repeatable target is the exception: its input name is checked against the EXPORT, by generate.normalise(), because the published graph no longer carries the keys that named it - removing them is what normalisation is.

schema.description: The artifact's own version. Bumped when the shape changes incompatibly.

source.description: Where this artifact came from, so a published copy traces back to a reviewed commit.

commit.description: Stamped at publication. Null means generated but not yet published, which is a valid state and not an error.

workflows.description: Keyed by the name a Job uses to ask for a Workflow. The key and the entry's own name must agree.

target.description: One place a Parameter's value is written into the graph. A target of a Parameter that emits a node per value carries the repeatable form instead: a slot pattern in `input`, the index it starts from in `from`, and how many of the values it takes in `take`. The pattern is declared rather than chosen by the engine because the two consumers of a reference image do not agree how a slot is named - one is `images.image_1`, the other `images.image0` - and a convention would be wrong for one of them silently.

input.description: An input the node declares. A dotted slot (images.image_1) is acceptable when its container is declared, because that is how an Autogrow input arrives. For a repeatable target this is a pattern whose {n} token stands for the value's position, spelled the way that node names its slots.

from.description: The index the pattern's first value takes: 1 for a container whose slots are image_1..., 0 for one whose slots are image0.... Required with a pattern and meaningless without one, because the base is a property of the node being written to and no default could be right for both.

take.description: How many of the supplied values this target receives. `all` writes one slot per value. `first` wires the target to the first emitted node alone, which is what a node comparing the result against the original needs; it is safe because the Parameter declares a floor, so there is always a first value to take. Declared on every target of an emitting Parameter rather than defaulted, so the artifact has one form and the engine has nothing to guess.

flexible.description: The node accepts a FAMILY of input names its own schema does not publish, and this target names that family. `Power Lora Loader (rgthree)` returns FlexibleOptionalInputType from INPUT_TYPES, so /object_info publishes `model` and `clip` and nothing else while `load_loras` reads every `lora_N` kwarg it is handed - measured at the SHA the Dockerfile pins, and unanswerable from this side of the seam. So the claim is authored here rather than derived, and it is honoured only where all three of these hold: the claim is on this target, the node's class IS the one named, and the name written is one this target's pattern expands to. A claim on the wrong node, the wrong class or the wrong spelling therefore fails generation and fails the Job rather than injecting a name nothing reads.

type.description: The caller's contract for the values a Job supplies. Not a Python type. `images` and `loras` are the two types the Worker ACTS on rather than reads. An `images` value is a picture, which cannot cross as a value at all: the Worker decodes each one, writes it into the engine's input directory before the graph is submitted, and puts the name it landed under into the node the declaration emits - so an `images` Parameter must also declare `emits`, and the token in that node's inputs stands for the uploaded name rather than the bytes (ADR-0009). A `loras` value is a URL and a strength: the Worker fetches the URL into a directory the engine already searches, and writes into each slot a structured value the declaration's `slot` template builds from the filename the fetch produced - so a `loras` Parameter must also declare `slot`, and a ceiling on one fetched file in `max_file_bytes`, because a Fetch is the one path where the caller rather than this repo names the machine the bytes come from (ADR-0011).

default.description: Applied when a Job omits the Parameter. Absent means the Parameter is required, which is the case for seed: the Worker resolves it, so a default would be a lie.

values.description: The exact set of values a Job may supply, and the `default` is required to be one of them. This exists because some node inputs are the ENGINE's enum rather than free text - `aspect_ratio`, `sampler_name` and `scheduler` are all combo widgets whose option list lives in the engine and is not published in the graph. A name outside the set is a KeyError inside the node's `execute`, so the run dies and the Job reports `generation_failed` naming nothing the caller can act on; declaring the set turns that into `invalid_request` naming the value, refused before submission and before a worker is paid. All three now carry it, `aspect_ratio` included - it was the first to go out without one and cost a billed Job to find out. The list is the engine's, transcribed at the pinned ComfyUI tag, so a tag bump makes it stale in the permissive direction - refusing a value the engine would have accepted - which is why a test pins each list's length.

min.description: The floor: the fewest values a Job may supply, refused before submission. Declared because zero is what the engine's container structurally allows and not what the Workflow means - an edit with no source is an edit of nothing, and a run that proceeded would return a plausible image with the intent silently ignored. Absent means the Parameter has no floor (ADR-0006's harm, and ADR-0002's dated correction to its own 'or none').

max.description: The ceiling: the most values a Job may supply, refused before submission naming the bound. Declared rather than derived because the bound is the engine container's, and /object_info describes a container without its expanded slot names - those are in the class's source, not in its published schema. For reference_images it is 16: the encoder's Autogrow container declares image_1..image_16, while the batch node feeding the enhancer declares min=1 max=50, and the smaller is the only bound that keeps every consumer looking at the same set. Above it the engine drops the extra slot in silence, so the encoder would ignore references the rest of the graph had already accepted.

emits.description: The node injection emits once per supplied value, which is what makes the Parameter repeatable rather than fixed. An emitted node whose class the engine does not provide, or whose id collides with one the graph already uses, is refused before submission.

inputs.description: The emitted node's inputs. The {value} token stands for the value that node was emitted from.

max_file_bytes.description: The largest ONE FILE a value of this Parameter may fetch, in bytes, refused before the body is read. A bound of a different kind from `min`/`max`, which count values: this one bounds one value's size, and it is required on a `loras` Parameter because the Worker fetches whatever URL the caller named. The caller chooses that URL, so an oversized file is the caller's own mistake and the Worker names both numbers rather than letting a host hold the Worker by dribbling bytes - a socket timeout bounds silence, not the total. Declared rather than fixed inside the fetch so the contract carries it: Civitai's metadata route is public and reports a file's size, so an interface can pre-check a LoRA before spending a Job on it. Absent means the Parameter does not fetch anything large, and the Worker refuses a `loras` Parameter that declares none rather than fetching unbounded.

slot.description: The object written into one slot per supplied value, for a Parameter whose values the Worker BUILDS rather than passes through. It is the sibling of `emits` and the other half of the same idea: `emits` says which node each value becomes, `slot` says what each value says where it lands. A string in the template is a template - {value} stands for the name the Worker's own act produced (the filename a Fetch wrote) and {strength} for the strength the Job asked for - and any other value is the constant it looks like, which is how a LoRA slot stays switched on. The template's keys are the TARGET NODE's vocabulary rather than this schema's, which is why they are not enumerated here; rgthree's loader skips any value missing `on`, `lora` or `strength`, in silence, so they are pinned by a test against the class's own source instead. A Parameter that declares `slot` writes a name per value, so every target must carry a slot pattern: there is no fixed input that could hold more than one.

targets.description: Where the value is written. Always a list, never a single node/input pair with a shorthand: a Workflow carrying the PE enhancer holds the caller's prompt in two places - the enhancer's own input and the switch branch the encoder reads when the enhancer is off - so writing only one of them silently ignores the caller.

version.description: The human label. It may stay the same across a real change, which is why graph_hash exists beside it.

graph_hash.description: SHA-256 over the graph alone, canonically serialised. Any node edit changes it; serialisation order does not.

graph.description: The Node graph in API format: a flat map from node id to a class type and its inputs.

preview_node.description: The node whose text output carries the prompt as the encoder finally received it. Present only for a Workflow with an enhancer.
